howDoI.q: How do I make a shop with things for sale, each with a price?
How do I make something that can be bought only once?
How do I make an exit that needs something bought?
How do I make things that cost different amounts?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Kit's Shop is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the level that say what you are looking at. It has one level and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the level is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your Money.

For the basic idea of paying, see Spend It, which has one stall. For points, see Coins and Score. For a door with a price, see Stronger Keys.

pages.head: Level 1: Kit's Shop
pages.html:
Level 1: Kit's Shop

Eight coins are in the street: six on the path and two up the ladder. Inside the shop three stalls stand in a row, each with its price on a card on its roof: a gold key (3), a silver key (3) and a heart (2). Walk into a stall to pay. It takes its price, hands over the item, and turns into a SOLD counter that does nothing more. Two gates in the far wall (silver, then gold) take a key each, so both keys are needed to leave. All three things cost eight, which is every coin, so the heart needs the two up the ladder.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the level is made

  • The coins. Open kitshop.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the cash block. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is 3 (Money) and Effect amount is 1. It has no score.
  • Three stalls, three prices. stall.key.3, stall.silver.3 and stall.heart.2 each have Effect counter 3 and an Effect amount of −3, −3 and −2. The picture on the roof (awning3, awning2) shows the price; the rule takes it. A touch is allowed only if the counter stays above zero, and a counter holds one more than the coins carried, so exactly three coins pay a price of three.
  • Too few. Walk into a stall with nothing left and nothing happens. The way through is to jump over it, or fetch more coins.
  • What you get. A block has one Effect counter and the price uses it, so each stall turns into another block when it is paid: give.key (adds 1 to counter 20), give.silver (adds 1 to counter 21) or give.heart (adds a life). They look like the SOLD counter and can be walked through, and they turn into sold as you take the item.
  • Bought once. A stall that has turned into sold has no rule left, so it cannot be bought again.
  • The exit. The blue silver gate takes one key from counter 21 and the brown gold gate takes one from counter 20, the same gates as in Stronger Keys. Both are in the way, so both keys must be bought.
  • The start. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Money (3) and the two key counters (20, 21) start at 1, which the game shows as none.
  • Choosing. Six coins on the path pay for both keys, but not the heart. The player buys the keys first and then climbs for the last two coins, or climbs first. The level does not say which.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

  • Nothing shows the number of coins left while you play. Money is counter 3, the one counter Game-Maker prints as a number, and only on the status page (F2). The prices are pictures you draw yourself.
  • A block has one Effect counter. The price uses it, so what you get has to come from the block the stall turns into. Each stall makes its own pair of blocks, a stall and a hand-over.
  • A shelf item cannot go back. There is no refund and no restocking in one visit; a stall is sold until you start the level again.
  • A price is fixed. There is no sale and no change given for a note.
  • Nothing stops a player jumping over a stall to reach the next one, which is why the level pays for the keys first and puts the heart last.
  • The heart gives a life, which the game shows only on the status page.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In kitshop.bbl, change stall.heart.2's Effect amount to −1. The heart is cheaper, though its card still says 2.
  • Copy stall.key.3, set its Effect amount to −5 and put it on the map. A more expensive key.
  • Take the ladder coins out of the map. Both keys can still be bought, and the heart cannot.
  • Change give.heart's Effect counter to counter 20. The heart stall now sells a gold key.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.tagline: Everything on the shelf has a price.
box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie gathers coins in the street and walks into a shop. A gold key and a silver key cost three each, a heart costs two, and the exit wants both keys. Each thing can be bought once, and then the stall says SOLD. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and set a price of your own.
features: Signs in the level explain each idea
Three stalls, each with its price on the roof
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: One level about a shop. Coins in the street add to your Money, and in the shop each thing on the shelf has a price on its roof: a gold key for three, a silver key for three and a heart for two. Pay and you get it, and the stall says SOLD; with too few coins, nothing happens. The exit is locked with two gates, so you need both keys. Signs say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and set a price of your own.
